fields.description:
## Context

The `tickets` pack grows ~2.0 KiB/commit at ~14K commits/day because each enrichment step
(ENQUEUE/CLAIM/DONE_ENRICH) and each `TICKET_DIGEST` is written as its OWN commit, re-emitting the
270 KB root tree every time. Below-horizon collapse (S1) removes the historical churn; W1 removes
the churn AT THE SOURCE so it does not re-accumulate, which is what keeps the pack under budget
after the reclaim lands.

## Scope

Batch the derived enrichment quartet + digest for a single logical mutation into ONE write/commit
(one root-tree re-emission) instead of 3-4, without changing observable ticket state, event
semantics, signatures, or optimistic-concurrency guarantees. Preserve per-event signing/verifiability.

## Out of scope

The history reclaim of already-accumulated commits (that is S1). No change to the event schema's
observable contract beyond commit batching.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single logical mutation that today emits the enrichment quartet + digest as separate commits emits ONE commit (one root-tree re-emission), measured on a fixture.
- [ ] Observable reduced ticket state is unchanged vs the pre-batch behavior (reducer-equality fixture passes).
- [ ] Each batched event retains its individual signature and passes `rebar verify-authorship`.
- [ ] Optimistic-concurrency / audit guarantees are preserved (existing concurrency tests pass).
- [ ] The measured commits-per-mutation and per-mutation root-tree re-emission count drop as designed.

## Portability

Pure library/store change; no dependence on any single CI provider.

## Implementation plan (2026-08-31)

### Mechanism

Use the existing in-process event batching seam instead of introducing a new event type or schema. The write path already has `_commands._seam.batch_sink()` (which still composes each event through the normal envelope, attribution, secret-screen, HLC timestamp, UUID, and authorship-signing path) and `_store.event_append.batch_write_and_push()` / `batch_stage_and_commit()` (which commits multiple prepared event files in one locked git commit and one push). W1 will route one enrichment write lane through those primitives.

1. Add an enrichment-local batch flush helper in `rebar.llm.enrich_drain` that opens a `_seam.batch_sink`, executes the queue/digest appends for one logical enrichment item, and flushes the resulting buffered `(ticket_id, event)` records with `_store.event_append.batch_write_and_push()`.
2. Use that helper for the success finalize path so `TICKET_DIGEST` and `DONE_ENRICH` land in one commit, while each event is still individually prepared/signed by the existing append seam before batching.
3. Where the drain itself creates derived queue events for the same item (self-heal stale-digest re-enqueue and optimistic claim), keep the claim-before-LLM concurrency boundary intact: do not defer a visible claim past the LLM call. If batching the claim with later writeback would weaken duplicate-spend prevention, keep the claim pre-LLM and document/test that concurrency semantics are unchanged rather than changing the queue contract.
4. Preserve failure behavior: if digest emission fails, enrichment remains best-effort and `DONE_ENRICH` is not falsely recorded as a completed enrichment for a missing digest. If a batched commit fails, the existing batch primitive rolls back the whole batch so no partial derived event is left staged/on disk.
5. Keep `enqueue`, `claim`, `mark_done`, and `digest_sidecar.emit` public contracts backward-compatible; any new helper is additive/private.

### Test plan / RED-first oracle

- Add a fixture-level regression test in `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py` that counts commits in the test tracker before and after one successful drain item and asserts the derived finalize write emits one additional commit containing both `TICKET_DIGEST` and `DONE_ENRICH` event files. The same test also counts root tree emissions via the commit count, proving reduced churn.
- Add/strengthen an observable-state test that compares reduced queue state and digest freshness after the batched path with the existing behavior's public postconditions: digest present/fresh, queue `pending == False`, `done == True`, and no schema-visible ticket-state change from the sidecar.
- Add a signing/verifiability assertion on the real fixture store using `rebar verify-authorship` so batched events prove individual authorship records still verify.
- Run existing concurrency coverage that owns claim arbitration and drain overlap: `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py::test_concurrent_drains_make_zero_duplicate_llm_calls` plus related stale/re-enqueue tests. This preserves optimistic-concurrency/audit behavior without adding a bespoke race harness because W1 reuses the existing single locked batch commit seam and does not add retry/backoff/cache logic.
- Preflight before push with the project gates (targeted pytest first, then `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test` if targeted gates are green).

### Surface-parity census

- CLI command: in scope through `rebar enrich --drain`/`cmd_enrich` because it routes to `enrich_drain.drain`; existing CLI dispatch test plus new drain regression covers the shared core.
- MCP/API tool: out of scope for a separate direct test; MCP enrichment surfaces call the same library drain/queue core and no MCP schema or output contract changes.
- Library facade/public import path: in scope through direct `rebar.llm.enrich_drain.drain`, `rebar.llm.overlap.queue`, and `digest_sidecar` fixture tests.
- Automated callers: in scope by preserving `_store.event_append.write_and_push -> _maybe_enrich_drain -> maybe_drain -> drain`; no caller-specific batching branch is introduced.
- Dual-direction/read mirrors: in scope through `latest_ticket_digest`, `digest_sidecar.freshness`, `queue.reduce_ticket`, and `pending_enrichment` assertions; read/event reducer contracts remain unchanged.

### Acceptance mapping

AC1/AC5 are proven by commit-count/root-tree emission tests on a fixture. AC2 is proven by reducer/reader equality-style public postconditions. AC3 is proven by `verify-authorship` on the fixture after batched writes. AC4 is proven by existing drain concurrency tests and by not moving the durable claim before the LLM boundary.
